source.title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a closed bounded convex subset B of L1[0,1] that is anti-proximinal, meaning that every point x in L1[0,1]\B has no nearest point in B? If such a set exists, can one choose B to have nonempty interior?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Does there exist an anti-proximinal closed bounded convex subset B in L1? What if we assume int (B) 6= ∅?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace R of L1[0,1] such that the quotient space L1[0,1]/R is isomorphic to L1[0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. ([37]) Does there exist an infinite dimensional reflexive subspace R of L1 such that L1/R isomorphic to L1?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space that can be realized as a subspace of L0 also embed into L1[0,1]?
accepted.context_brief: embedding Banach subspaces of L0 into L1

evidence.quote: Problem 3. (Kwapień, [119]) Does every Banach subspace of L0 embed in L1?

accepted.question_text: For every infinite-dimensional subspace X of L1[0,1], does there exist a decomposition L1[0,1] = Y ⊕ Z in which both Y and Z are isomorphic to L1[0,1] and both intersections X∩Y and X∩Z are infinite-dimensional?
accepted.context_brief: placing subspaces inside two L1 summands

evidence.quote: Problem 4. ([19]) Does every infinite dimensional subspace X ⊂ L1 admits a decomposition L1 = Y ⊕Z into subspaces Y and Z , both isomorphic to L1 such that both X ∩Y and X ∩Z are infinite dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1[0,1] isomorphic either to L1[0,1] itself or to ℓ1? Equivalently, is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1[0,1] isomorphic to some L1(ν)-space?
accepted.context_brief: classification of complemented subspaces of L1

evidence.quote: Problem 5. ([79]) Is every (infinite dimensional) complemented subspace of L1 isomorphic to either L1 or `1 (equivalently, to an L1(ν)-space)?

accepted.question_text: What is the largest constant λ such that every subspace X of L1[0,1] that is λ-isomorphic to some L1(ν)-space must be complemented in L1[0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. ([10]) What is the maximal value of λ such that if X is a subspace of L1 which is λ-isomorphic to some L1(ν) then X is complemented in L1?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist δ > 0 such that every separable L1,1+ε-space with ε ≤ δ is isomorphic to an L1(ν)-space, and if so does the optimal isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0? Likewise, does there exist δ > 0 such that every (1+ε)-complemented subspace of L1[0,1] with ε ≤ δ is isomorphic to an L1(ν)-space, and if so does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. ([4]) (i) Does there exist a δ > 0 such that every separable L1,1+ε-space is isomorphic to an L1(ν) for ε ≤ δ? If yes then does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0? (ii) Does there exist a δ > 0 such that every (1 + ε)- complemented subspace of L1 is isomorphic to an L1(ν) for ε ≤ δ? If yes then does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist ε1 > 0 such that whenever X is a complemented subspace of L1[0,1] and Y is a subspace of L1[0,1] with Banach-Mazur distance d(Y,X) < 1+ε for some ε ≤ ε1, the space Y must also be complemented? If so, how is the projection constant of Y controlled by the projection constant of X, possibly with ε1 depending on that projection constant?
accepted.context_brief: stability of complementability under small distortion

evidence.quote: Problem 8. [B. Randrianantoanina] Does there exists an ε1 > 0 such that whenever X is a complemented subspace of L1 and Y is a subspace of L1 with d(Y,X) < 1 + ε with ε ≤ ε1 , then Y is complemented? If yes, how is the projection constant of Y related to that of X ? Maybe, ε1 depending on the projection constant K of X ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a normalized Schauder basis of L1[0,1] that can be partitioned into two subsequences such that one subsequence is relatively weakly compact and the other is equivalent to the unit vector basis of ℓ1?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. [116] Does there exist a normalized basis of L1 which can be split into two subsequences, one of which forms a relatively weakly compact set and second is equivalent to the unit vector basis of `1?

accepted.question_text: If X is a subspace of a possibly non-separable L1(μ)-space, must X contain an unconditional basic sequence whose cardinality equals dens(X), the density character of X?
accepted.context_brief: large unconditional basic sequences in L1(mu)

evidence.quote: Problem 10. ([100, p.38]) Does every subspace X ⊆ L1(μ) contain an unconditional basic sequence of cardinality densX ?

accepted.question_text: Let 1 < s < p ≤ ∞. Must every bounded linear operator T: Lp → L1 factor through Ls, meaning that there exist bounded operators S: Lp → Ls and U: Ls → L1 with T = U ∘ S?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. ([77]) Let 1

accepted.question_text: If X is a subspace of L1[0,1] such that the quotient L1[0,1]/X is isomorphic to c0, must X have the Dunford-Pettis property?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. ([66]) Suppose X is a subspace of L1 with L1/X isomorphic to c0. Does X have the Dunford-Pettis property?

accepted.question_text: Is every projection P on L1[0,1] that is L1-singular, meaning that it does not fix any subspace isomorphic to L1[0,1], necessarily a Dunford-Pettis operator?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. ([107], [31] and [9]) Is every L1-singular projection P ∈ L(L1) a Dunford-Pettis operator?

accepted.question_text: Suppose L1[0,1] sign-embeds into a Banach space X. Must L1[0,1] then Gδ-embed into X? Suppose instead that L1[0,1] Gδ-embeds into X. Must L1[0,1] semi-embed into X? More generally, does sign-embedding of L1[0,1] into X already imply semi-embedding of L1[0,1] into X?
accepted.context_brief: relations among weak embeddings of L1

evidence.quote: Problem 14. A) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds into X . Does L1 Gδ -embed into X ? B) Suppose that L1 Gδ -embeds into X . Does L1 semi-embed into X ? C) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds into X . Does L1 semi-embed into X ?

accepted.question_text: Assume L1[0,1] Gδ-embeds into a Banach space X and Y is a subspace of X. Must L1[0,1] Gδ-embed into Y or into the quotient X/Y? Likewise, if L1[0,1] semi-embeds into X and Y is a subspace of X, must L1[0,1] semi-embed into Y or into X/Y?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. A) Suppose that L1 Gδ -embeds into a Banach space X and let Y be a subspace of X . Does L1 Gδ -embed either into Y or into X/Y ? B) Suppose that L1 semi-embeds into a Banach space X and let Y be a subspace of X . Does L1 semi-embed either into Y or into X/Y ?

accepted.question_text: Let P = {x ∈ L1[0,1] : x ≥ 0 and ||x|| = 1}, the positive face of the unit sphere of L1[0,1]. If T: L1[0,1] → X is a bounded linear operator such that T(P) is closed, must T be a semi-embedding, that is, must T be injective with T(B(L1[0,1])) closed?
accepted.context_brief: closed image of the positive face

evidence.quote: Problem 16. [14] Suppose that T ∈ L(L1, X) is such that TP is closed. Must T be a semi-embedding?

accepted.question_text: Fix a reflexive subspace E of L1[0,1]. If a bounded linear operator T: L1[0,1] → X fixes no copy of E, does it follow that T is narrow?

evidence.quote: Problem 17. ([100]) Let E be a reflexive subspace of L1. Suppose that T ∈ L(L1, X) fixes no copy of E . Does it follow that T is narrow? This is unknown for any E .

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Banach space X, is the sum of two narrow operators from L1[0,1] to X again a narrow operator?
accepted.context_brief: stability of narrow operators under addition

evidence.quote: Problem 18. ([59]) For each Banach space X , is the sum of two narrow operators from L1 to X also narrow?

accepted.question_text: Is every KSW-narrow operator from L1[0,1] to an arbitrary Banach space X necessarily narrow in the earlier sense of narrow operators on L1?
accepted.context_brief: comparison of KSW-narrow and narrow operators

evidence.quote: Problem 19. ([62]) Is every KSW-narrow operator from L1 to X narrow?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Banach space X, is the sum of two KSW-narrow operators in L(L1[0,1], X) again KSW-narrow?
accepted.context_brief: stability of KSW-narrow operators under addition

evidence.quote: Problem 20. ([59]) For any Banach space X , is the sum of two KSW-narrow operators from L(L1, X) also KSW-narrow (cf. Problem 18)?

accepted.question_text: Is every Tauberian operator T: L1[0,1] → L1[0,1] a semi-Fredholm operator?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Is every Tauberian operator T : L1 −→ L1 a semi-Fredholm operator?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the Matematychni Studii PDF and mapped sections 1-9 with numbered Problems 1-21 on pages 2-14.
Extracted all explicit numbered problem statements from the PDF; no solved labels were present in the source artifact.
Rewrote each numbered problem into self-contained form by expanding source-specific terminology only when supported by nearby definitions in the paper.
No duplicates were merged; Problems 7, 14, and 15 were kept as single multi-part questions because the source presents each as one numbered problem.
All accepted items have direct verbatim evidence with page numbers and passed self-containedness and no-new-facts checks.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/some-open-problems-on-the-classical-function-space-l1.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
